policy.large_source_policy: Materialize into hero/assets/source/ (ignored) via a recorded fetch; never commit large provider rasters or render sequences.

license_basis_notes.copernicus-open-access: Copernicus Sentinel data: free, full and open access under the Legal Notice on the use of Copernicus Sentinel Data and Service Information; any use must state 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [year]'. Commercial use permitted.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Visible Earth, Blue Marble Next Generation series)
assets.notes: Whole-Earth true-color composite (land, ocean, sea ice, clouds baked in), 2048x1024 equirectangular. Used as the day-side albedo/base-color input and cloud registration reference for the Earth material. Not a measured scientific layer; carries no forbidden layer class. Attribution: NASA Earth Observatory.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Visible Earth, Blue Marble Next Generation series)
assets.notes: The 8192x4096 member of the same NASA Visible Earth image record (57735) as earth_day_composite, fetched from the same host under the same public-domain policy. Same scene, same clouds, same equirectangular 2:1 projection and same geography at four times the linear resolution, so the accepted world-coordinate convention and the AOI's configured longitude offset carry over unchanged; only sampling density differs. Introduced for WEB-HERO-001D because the 2048 px asset magnifies about fourteen times at the regional approach and visibly softens. Not a measured scientific layer; carries no forbidden layer class. Attribution: NASA Earth Observatory.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Suomi NPP VIIRS Day-Night Band, Earth at Night 2012 / Black Marble series)
assets.notes: Whole-Earth city-lights composite, 3600x1800 equirectangular. Used as the night-side emission input, blended in only on the unlit hemisphere via a scripted terminator factor. Not a measured scientific layer; carries no forbidden layer class. Attribution: NASA Earth Observatory.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Blue Marble: Next Generation, July 2004, with topography and bathymetry; produced by Reto Stoeckli, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center)
assets.third_party_restrictions: None on the record: NASA-produced from MODIS observations with USGS/NGDC topography and bathymetry shading; no third-party copyright noted.
assets.notes: WEB-005A R2 global Earth albedo (A-HERO-11). Cloud-free monthly composite at about 2 km per texel; the regional detail window below sits inside it. Same equirectangular 2:1 projection and same geography as the accepted composite, so the accepted world-coordinate convention and the AOI's configured longitude offset carry over unchanged. Cinematic Earth/context texture only; not an OrbGSS analytical raster, not a sensor-specific observation, carries no forbidden layer class. No NASA insignia is used and no endorsement is implied. Attribution: NASA Earth Observatory.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Blue Marble: Next Generation, July 2004, with topography and bathymetry; produced by Reto Stoeckli, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center)
assets.third_party_restrictions: None on the record; same dataset and credit as earth_bmng_global_2km.
assets.notes: Full-resolution 500 m tile C1 of the same NASA record, covering longitude 0-90 E and latitude 0-90 N, which contains the accepted Kizildere regional frame. Materialized only as the source of the regional detail crop below; it is not loaded by the renderer itself.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Blue Marble: Next Generation, July 2004, with topography and bathymetry); crop by OrbGSS
assets.third_party_restrictions: None; a crop of a NASA public-domain tile.
assets.notes: WEB-005A R2 regional detail window (A-HERO-11): the texture the regional approach and hold actually resolve. About 464 m per texel (about 365 m east-west at the AOI latitude), against 3856 m in the rejected checkpoint. Blended into the global albedo over a 2.5 degree feather by the Earth material; presentation only.

assets.publisher: NASA Earth Observatory (Blue Marble: Clouds; Blue Marble Next Generation series)
assets.third_party_restrictions: None on the record; NASA-produced cloud composite.
assets.notes: Greyscale cloud composite mixed over the cloud-free BMNG albedo by the Earth material. This is the same cloud layer the accepted land_ocean_ice_cloud composite (record 57735) was assembled from, which is what keeps the R2 global look continuous with the accepted one. July 2004 cover is nearly clear over western Anatolia, so nothing is faded or painted around the target.

assets.publisher: European Union, Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission (ESA); detail ratio derived by OrbGSS
assets.acquisition: 2025-09-25, tiles T35SPC and T35SPB, cloudy pixels 0.001-0.002 percent, no snow
assets.third_party_restrictions: None beyond the Copernicus attribution requirement, which is carried by the site footer.
assets.notes: WEB-005A R3 regional detail multiplier: a greyscale ratio texture with no units and no palette that the Earth material multiplies into the Blue Marble albedo under the regional hold, so 30 m ground structure appears without any colour or seasonal change. Presentation only: not an OrbGSS analytical raster, not a sensor-specific claim on the page, carries no forbidden layer class, never delivered to the site. The Sentinel-2 source tiles are not copied into this repository; they are the science project's raw archive and are identified by name and SHA-256 above.

notes: WEB-HERO-001A shipped a fully procedural benchmark scene with no external asset. WEB-HERO-001B introduces the two Earth composites above for the day/night material; both are NASA public-domain whole-Earth imagery (not measured science-layer output), fetched directly from eoimages.gsfc.nasa.gov and checksummed. The satellite, atmosphere, and starfield in WEB-HERO-001B remain fully procedural and introduce no further external asset. WEB-HERO-001C adds the surface-conforming AOI acquisition system (footprint, border, corner locks, scan beams and scan sweep) and introduces no new external asset: all of it is generated procedurally from committed configuration by hero/scripts/aoi_system.py, and none of it encodes, derives or displays a scientific quantity. WEB-HERO-001D introduces no new class of external material: it adds the 8192 px member of the already-cleared NASA Visible Earth Blue Marble record as the Earth albedo for the closest-approach sharpness gate, and keeps the 2048 px asset recorded because the accepted Phase-B and Phase-C scenes still reference it and must stay reproducible. The refined two-shell atmosphere limb, the constraint-locked camera and every AOI element remain fully procedural, generated from committed configuration, and none of them encodes, derives or displays a scientific quantity. WEB-005A R2 adds the NASA Blue Marble Next Generation global albedo, its 500 m C1 tile and an OrbGSS lossless crop of that tile as the regional detail window, plus the NASA Blue Marble cloud composite, all NASA public-domain whole-Earth imagery fetched from eoimages.gsfc.nasa.gov and checksummed, materialized under the Earth-source-resolution authority of WEB-005A (A-HERO-11). The satellite model remains fully procedural (hero/scripts/satellite_model.py) and introduces no external asset. The accepted 2048/8192 composites stay recorded because the accepted scenes still reference them.
